learningObjectives.title: The nature of God and the Trinity

questions.q: The three persons of the Christian Trinity are:
options: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit
The Father, the Mother and the Child
The Creator, the Prophet and the Angel
questions.explain: Christians describe God as one being in three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: In describing God, the term 'omnipotent' means:
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful, expressing the belief that God has unlimited power.
Omnibenevolent means all-loving or all-good, a key attribute of God in Christian belief.

options: God becoming human in the person of Jesus
The creation of the world in six days
The resurrection of Jesus from the dead
The gift of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
questions.explain: The incarnation is the belief that God took on human form and nature in Jesus Christ.

questions.q: Which historic statement of faith sets out the Christian belief in the Trinity?
questions.explain: The Nicene Creed affirms belief in one God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Which parable of Jesus is most often linked to the idea of the Last Judgement?
questions.explain: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, people are judged and separated according to how they treated others.
Omniscient means all-knowing, the belief that God knows everything, past, present and future.

questions.q: The doctrine of the Trinity teaches that:
options: There is one God who exists as three persons
God changes between three roles at different times
God is only the Father, with Jesus and the Spirit being angels
questions.explain: The Trinity means one God in three distinct but united persons, not three gods.

questions.q: Christians believe the incarnation is significant because it shows that:
options: God fully entered human life and experience in Jesus
God has no involvement with the world
Jesus was only a human teacher
The world came about purely by chance
questions.explain: The incarnation shows God sharing fully in human life, making God close to and understanding of humanity.

questions.q: In Christian teaching, 'original sin' refers to:
options: The tendency to sin inherited as a result of the Fall of Adam and Eve
The first sin a person commits as an adult
A sin that can never be forgiven
A sin committed only by non-believers
questions.explain: Original sin is the belief that humanity inherits a sinful nature stemming from the Fall in Genesis.

options: Jesus' death restoring the relationship between God and humanity
The moment God created the universe
The final judgement of all souls
The gift of tongues at Pentecost
questions.explain: Atonement is the belief that Jesus' death makes amends for human sin and reconciles people to God.

questions.q: Many Christians teach that salvation is received primarily through:
options: God's grace, accepted through faith in Jesus
Perfectly keeping every law without ever failing
questions.explain: Salvation is widely understood as a free gift of God's grace, received through faith rather than earned.

questions.q: The 'problem of evil' challenges belief in God because:
options: Suffering seems hard to reconcile with a God who is all-powerful and all-loving
It proves that God is all-knowing
It shows that God wants people to be good
It demonstrates the world was perfectly designed
questions.explain: If God is omnipotent and omnibenevolent, the existence of suffering raises the question of why God allows it.

questions.q: In Catholic teaching, purgatory is understood as:
options: A state of purification before entering heaven
The place where God created humans
The garden where Adam and Eve lived
questions.explain: Catholics believe purgatory is a state in which souls are purified before they can enter heaven.

questions.q: A Christian comforts a suffering friend by saying 'God still cares for you.' This response most directly draws on the belief that God is:
questions.explain: The reassurance of God's care reflects the belief that God is omnibenevolent, or all-loving.

questions.q: A Christian argues that death is not the end because Jesus was raised from the dead. This reasoning is based on the:
questions.explain: Belief in life after death is grounded in the resurrection of Jesus, seen as a promise of eternal life.

questions.q: Guided by the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, a Christian volunteers to help homeless people. This shows the belief that:
options: People will be judged by how they treated others
Only belief matters and actions are irrelevant
There will be no judgement after death
Wealth guarantees a place in heaven
questions.explain: The parable teaches that judgement is linked to how people cared for those in need.

questions.q: A Christian says Jesus can understand human temptation because he was fully human as well as fully God. This belief comes from the doctrine of the:
questions.explain: The incarnation holds that Jesus is both fully divine and fully human, so he shares human experience.
